feed.title: Aadesh Ingle
feed.subtitle: Aadesh Ingle, founding engineer building production AI systems (agents, RAG, voice, evals). Writing on shipping reliable AI, deep learning, and the craft of engineering.

entry.title: Stop Being the Thing Inside the Loop
entry.summary: Everyone says agent loop and means something different: a cron job, a retry, a while-true around a prompt. Here's the anatomy of a loop that actually ships work, and why the loop itself is the least valuable part.

entry.title: Golden Cases Come From Funerals
entry.summary: People ask where our eval test cases come from, expecting a methodology. The honest answer: every one of them is the gravestone of something that hurt us once.

entry.title: The Model Is the Easy Part
entry.summary: Across every AI product I've shipped, the model call was a few hundred lines. Everything that made it a product, the guardrails, evals, observability, and workflow, was everything else.

entry.title: The First Two Weeks Are for Listening
entry.summary: The most expensive mistake in client AI work happens before any code is written: solving the wrong problem brilliantly. The defense is unfashionable. Sit with the people doing the work.

entry.title: Evals Are the Operating System
entry.summary: Our AI agent negotiates freight loads over email with real brokers. When it gets one wrong, that's not a demo bug. It's real margin. Here's how we stopped judging it by vibes.

entry.title: The Bug Was in the Transcript
entry.summary: When a voice agent fails, you don't get a stack trace. You get a transcript, a tool log, and a complaint. The discipline is reading them in the right order.

entry.title: Trading Voice Quality for Reliability
entry.summary: Candidates were dropping out of voice conversations because the agent couldn't reliably do what they asked. The fix wasn't a better prompt. It was admitting the architecture was wrong.

entry.title: Three Thousand WhatsApp Messages a Day
entry.summary: A logistics customer's demand was arriving as messy, multilingual WhatsApp messages and emails, captured by hand. The LLM extraction was the easy part. The pipeline around it was the product.

entry.title: Where the Human Belongs in the Loop
entry.summary: Human-in-the-loop gets praised as the responsible default. Built carelessly, it's just a slower process with better branding: a human in the way, learning nothing.

entry.title: Writing Down What You Didn't Measure
entry.summary: Every project I run keeps a small file of claims and their evidence. The most useful column is the one that says: this number is an estimate, and here's what it would take to know.

entry.title: Demos Close Deals. Boring Systems Keep Them.
entry.summary: Ninety days after the contract is signed, nobody remembers the demo. What clients judge you on after that is everything the demo carefully avoided.

entry.title: What Actually Happens When You Call an LLM API
entry.summary: Most teams model it as prompt in, answer out. Then a 429 hits, or latency doubles at peak hours, and the mental model runs out. Here's the version that survives production.

entry.title: Running Two Model Providers in Production
entry.summary: We run OpenAI and Gemini side by side across client deployments. The myth I believed going in: prompts are portable. The thing that's actually portable: evals.

entry.title: Own the Failure Before It Becomes a Story
entry.summary: A friend's heartbreak reminded me that failure only becomes useful after it becomes specific. Pain is not the teacher. The record you make while it still hurts is.

entry.title: Why Output Tokens Cost More Than Input
entry.summary: Every provider's pricing page shows the same asymmetry: output tokens cost several times what input tokens do. It isn't margin games. It's physics, and it should change how you build.

entry.title: Principles I Reread Before Starting Anything New
entry.summary: Six things I keep relearning the expensive way, written down so the next project starts from the scar instead of the lesson.

entry.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Cleaning Data
entry.summary: Everyone wanted to talk about LLMs that quarter. I spent it on fuzzy matching and duplicate records, and it was some of the highest-leverage work I've done.

entry.title: BLEU Lies
entry.summary: My image captioning model scored ROUGE-L 39 and BLEU 10.3. One of those numbers made it sound competent and one made it sound broken. Reading the actual captions told a third story.

entry.title: Search for Languages the Internet Forgot
entry.summary: Dense retrieval works beautifully when you have the web's worth of training data. My thesis problem was what happens when you don't, when the language you're searching barely exists online.
